arxiv-1410-8481.title: Quantum versus classical polarons in a ferromagnetic CuO 3 -like chain
arxiv-1410-8481.creator: Krzysztof Bieniasz, Andrzej M. Oleś
arxiv-1410-8481.description: Abstract We present an exact solution for an itinerant hole added into the oxygen orbitals of a CuO 3 -like ferromagnetic chain. Using the Green’s function method, the quantum polarons obtained for the Heisenberg SU(2) interaction between localized Cu spins are compared with the polarons in the Ising chain.

arxiv-2009-11727.title: Evolution of Coordination in Pairwise and Multi-player Interactions via Prior Commitments
arxiv-2009-11727.creator: Ndidi Bianca Ogbo, Aiman Elgarig, The Anh Han
arxiv-2009-11727.description: Abstract Abstract Upon starting a collective endeavour, it is important to understand your partners’ preferences and how strongly they commit to a common goal. Establishing a prior commitment or agreement in terms of posterior benefits and consequences from those engaging in it provides an important mechanism for securing cooperation.

arxiv-2105-03978.title: Manipulating single photon emitter radiative lifetime in transition-metal dichalcogenides through Förster resonance energy transfer to graphene
arxiv-2105-03978.creator: R.Eddhib 1, S.Ayari 1, A.Hichri 1, S.Jaziri 1 , 2
arxiv-2105-03978.description: Abstract Structural defects can crucially impact the optical response of monolayer (ML) thick materials as they enable trapping sites for excitons. These trapped excitons appear in photoluminescence spectra as new emissions below the free bright exciton and it can be exploited for single photon emissions (SPE).

arxiv-2110-12260.title: Adaptive control of underactuated planar pronking hexapod
arxiv-2110-12260.creator: Güner Dilşad Er
arxiv-2110-12260.description: Abstract Abstract Underactuated legged robots depict highly nonlinear and complex dynamical behaviors that create significant challenges in accurately modeling system dynamics using both first principles and system identification approaches. Hence, it makes a more substantial challenge to design stabilizing controllers.

arxiv-2410-04424.title: DAdEE : Unsupervised Domain Adaptation in Early Exit PLMs
arxiv-2410-04424.creator: Divya Jyoti Bajpai, Manjesh Kumar Hanawal
arxiv-2410-04424.description: Abstract Pre-trained Language Models (PLMs) exhibit good accuracy and generalization ability across various tasks using self-supervision, but their large size results in high inference latency. Early Exit (EE) strategies handle the issue by allowing the samples to exit from classifiers attached to the intermediary layers, but they do not generalize well, as exit classifiers can be sensitive to domain changes.

arxiv-2410-18946.title: A geometric characterization of steady laminar flow
arxiv-2410-18946.creator: Theodore D. Drivas, Marc Nualart
arxiv-2410-18946.description: Abstract . We study the steady states of the Euler equations on the periodic channel or annulus. We show that if these flows are laminar (layered by closed non-contractible streamlines which foliate the domain), then they must be either parallel or circular flows. We also show that a large subset of these shear flows are isolated from non-shear stationary states.

arxiv-2501-04144.creator: Kam Woh Ng, Jing Yang, Jia Wei Sii, Chee Seng Chan, Jiankang Deng, Yi-Zhe Song, Tao Xiang, Xiatian Zhu

Understanding and generating the fine-grained structure of objects – such as birds with species-specific beaks, wings, and tails – is a long-standing challenge in computer vision.

pmc-10713901.title: Significance and current approaches to vascular graft infection
pmc-10713901.creator: Carlos–Alberto Mestres, Mathias Van Hemelrijck, Eduard Quintana, Francis Edwin Smit
pmc-10713901.description: Vascular graft/endograft infection (VGEI) is a constant in cardiovascular surgery with published rates between 1 and 5%. Every graft type and anatomical location is a potential target for infectious complications. These patients are sick patients with high frailty burden. Management of VGEI entails a multidisciplinary and multimodality approach.

pmc-12612547.title: Making sense of pediatric death: An exploratory qualitative study of emotion management strategies applied by the pediatric intensive care unit interprofessional team
pmc-12612547.creator: Lisa Albrecht, Molly J. Ryan, Eva Ta, Jennifer R. Foster, Laura Buckley, Hillary Ferguson, Kathy Lyons, Amanda van Beinum, Karen Dryden-Palmer
pmc-12612547.description: Background:Caring for children at the end of life is a reality of practice in the pediatric intensive care unit (PICU). Learning how to make sense of death at work, and the emotions it entails, is necessary for all PICU professionals.Objective:To explore how PICU clinicians manage their emotions when encountering pediatric death at work.

pmc-13400293.title: Obesity and severe obesity prevalence among youth aged 2–17 in Minnesota, 2020–2025
pmc-13400293.creator: Samuel T. Patnoe, Gabriela Vazquez-Benitez, Kelly R. Bergmann, Gretchen J. Buchanan, Michael Arenson, Summer L. Martins, Tyler N.A. Winkelman, Elyse O. Kharbanda
pmc-13400293.description: ObjectiveExisting sources for monitoring pediatric obesity prevalence are limited by delayed data availability and insufficient granularity for small-area estimates. We used data from the Minnesota Electronic Health Record Consortium's Health Trends Across Communities (HTAC) project to estimate obesity and severe obesity prevalence among Minnesota youth.MethodsIn serial cross-sectional analyses, HTAC data were obtained from 11 health systems in Minnesota.

pmc-13554048.title: Extracellular vesicles for next-gen therapeutics and drug delivery
pmc-13554048.creator: Nawaz Khan, Zeynab Ahmadova, Yujie Shi, Tayyab Shafiq, Yujie Liang, Li Duan
pmc-13554048.description: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) are membrane-bound, nano-sized particles released by diverse cell types. They serve as key mediators of intercellular communication by transporting a broad repertoire of proteins, lipids, nucleic acids, and metabolites to recipient cells within a protective lipid bilayer.

uslaw-usc-t42-s7153.description: United States Code, Title 42 (The Public Health And Welfare); Chapter 84 (Department Of Energy); Subchapter III (Transfers Of Functions). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) Authority retained by Secretary of the Interior The Secretary of the Interior shall retain any authorities not transferred under section 7152(b) 1 of this title and shall be solely responsible for the issuance and supervision of.
